summary: Profiles fixes: inactive slot chips now resolve key names through the runtime's physical_key_name resolver instead of a scan-code fallback, and the rename field takes the typed text's width in the same frame instead of scrolling on the stale state name. Both fixes ship with egui_kittest widget regression tests and the full gate passes.

PROFILE-RENAME-JITTER.evidence: rename_field now renders its TextEdit with clip_text(false): egui's singleline scroll-to-caret is disabled and the widget takes the live galley width in the keystroke's own frame instead of the one-frame-stale committed name, so the box grows rightward and the text never shifts. Widget test ui::profiles::tests::the_rename_field_takes_the_typed_texts_width_in_the_typing_frame passes (the field rect covers the typed text on the typing frame); before the fix the same test measured a 97.6px rect against 204.3px typed text and failed. The scoped loop and full gate passed.

PROFILE-INACTIVE-KEY-NAMES.evidence: chip resolves keys absent from the active draft's snapshot.keys through physical_key_name, the same resolver the runtime fills wire names with, replacing the SC:xx/E0:xx scan-code fallback. Widget test ui::profiles::tests::an_inactive_slots_chip_names_a_key_the_active_draft_no_longer_binds renders a draft remapped to Right Shift (0x36) while inactive slots keep W (0x11) and asserts zero SC:11 labels, at least three chips carrying the platform name, and the wire name still winning for the draft binding; before the fix the same test found three SC:11 chips and failed. The scoped loop and full gate passed.

risks: docs/architecture/ui.md (Profile slots section) still documents the SC:xx scan-code fallback and states that no platform name call is added to the settings process; that owner-doc sentence is stale after this fix and is outside this task's owned files, so updating the owning contract remains a Master/owner follow-up.

Both fixes are verified by widget tests and the full gate, not by native on-screen inspection; the stage's native-visual gap in docs/architecture/verification.md (Unverified Areas) remains for the rename box and the profile chips.

Chip labels now resolve at render time through the platform key-name call, so a keyboard-layout change while the settings window is open could relabel keys that are not in the current draft before the next snapshot refreshes the wire names; keys named by the snapshot keep the snapshot name.
